content.comment_body: Hello, I am experiencing an issue with [product_name] [version_no] and the [product_name] module. Previously, using [version_no], everything functioned well. After upgrading to [version_no] and updating the module's firmware, the module works but I can no longer establish a connection while it's connected (password currently disabled). If I disconnect the cable, it works. I've set up my network but am unsure how to add the module since it's not listed. Appreciate any help.

You do not need to add the [product_name] module as a compatible device in your network view. Instead, configure the module by specifying its connection to [product_name] [version_no] and entering its IP address in the module's settings. Additional configuration steps are required; please refer to the attachment for details.

So it's correct that two simultaneous connections are not possible. Where is this documented? For further details, check the section on general functions in the manual (see page 60). This means I should be able to stop module communication online without disconnecting any cables. Thank you.
You can find the information you need in the PDF attachment I mentioned earlier. My suggestion: Read the current manual. You can download the latest manual from [url].

To my knowledge, neither [product_name] nor the module can start or stop directly from the device interface. Also, I am not aware of any settings within the module that enable timed start/stop options.

The setup is now working. It's not possible to start or stop the module from within the software; there's no indication that you have stopped it. If you overlook this, you won't receive notifications, though you can schedule the module to auto-start, for example, every two hours. Thanks. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering challenges with configuring and managing connectivity between [product_name] [version_no] and its communication module after upgrading software and firmware. Changes in connection setup and absence of direct software controls for starting and stopping the module cause confusion and disrupt workflow. Documentation lacks clear guidance on newly required configurations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to easily configure and control communication modules entirely through their usual software, including establishing network connectivity and managing module operations online without manual actions like disconnecting cables.
